stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two maps. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1784, cartographer Ilse Varnhagen published a map of the Oder River delta.
• Varnhagen's map was engraved on copper plates and covered about 900 square kilometers.
• She gathered her measurements by walking the delta with a surveyor's chain.
• In 1791, cartographer Tomas Rečka published a map of the Morava floodplain.
• Rečka's map was printed from carved woodblocks and covered about 2,400 square kilometers.
• Rečka measured the floodplain on foot, pacing the land with a surveyor's chain.
choices: Varnhagen's map of the Oder delta was engraved on copper, whereas Rečka's map of the Morava floodplain was printed from woodblocks.
Both Varnhagen's 1784 map and Rečka's 1791 map were based on measurements taken on foot with a surveyor's chain.
Varnhagen's map covered about 900 square kilometers, less than half the area shown on Rečka's map of the Morava floodplain.
Varnhagen gathered the measurements for her 1784 map of the Oder River delta by walking the land with a surveyor's chain.
explanation: The two blocks of notes differ on printing method and area, but they share one feature: each cartographer measured the land on foot with a surveyor's chain. Choice B names both maps and uses 'both' to state that shared feature, so it does the job the goal asks for.

A.why: You picked an accurate detail, but 'whereas' marks a difference in printing method. The goal asked for a similarity, and this choice gives a contrast.

C.why: The arithmetic is right (900 is less than half of 2,400), but comparing sizes points out how the maps differ. It doesn't show anything they have in common.

D.why: This is the shared feature, but you only get it for Varnhagen. The sentence never says that Rečka worked the same way, so it doesn't establish a similarity.

choices: The Velmora program brought measles vaccines to villages in mobile clinics, while the Port Asher program offered them in public libraries.
In its first year, the Velmora program reached about 14,000 children, more than twice as many as the Port Asher program reached.
Both the Velmora and Port Asher programs offered measles vaccines to children living in rural villages far from hospitals.

B.why: The figures are accurate, but setting 14,000 against 6,500 shows how the programs differ in size. It doesn't show what they share.

C.why: Port Asher is a city whose program ran in public libraries, so 'rural villages' is true only of Velmora. You took a feature of one program and applied it to both.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the results of the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

• Agronomist Dalia Ferreira tested crimson clover as a winter cover crop on Iowa cornfields.
• The clover added nitrogen to the soil, reducing the fertilizer needed the next season.
• Clover-planted fields lost about 40 percent less topsoil to erosion than bare fields.
• Agronomist Kwame Oduya tested winter rye as a cover crop on Ohio soybean fields.
• The rye added no nitrogen but suppressed weeds the following spring.
• Rye-planted fields lost about 45 percent less topsoil to erosion than bare fields.
choices: In both studies, the fields planted with a winter cover crop lost at least 40 percent less topsoil to erosion than bare fields did.
Unlike winter rye, which suppressed weeds in spring, crimson clover added nitrogen to the soil and reduced the need for fertilizer.
Both crimson clover and winter rye added nitrogen to the soil, reducing the amount of fertilizer farmers needed the next season.
Ferreira found that planting crimson clover on Iowa cornfields reduced topsoil erosion by about 40 percent compared with bare fields.
explanation: The two studies found different secondary benefits, but both found less erosion: 40 percent for clover and 45 percent for rye. Choice A covers both studies with one accurate statement ('at least 40 percent') and uses 'in both studies' to make the shared result explicit.

B.why: This falls for the subtype's trap. It is a detailed and accurate sentence, but 'unlike' shows that it is about a difference between the crops.

C.why: The notes say the rye 'added no nitrogen.' You took a result from the clover study and applied it to both.

D.why: This states the shared result for Ferreira's study only. It never says that Oduya found the same thing, so no similarity is drawn.

stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Folklorist Ines Marwood recorded 212 versions of "The Salt Bride," a tale from coastal villages in northern Portugal.
• Most versions of "The Salt Bride" end with the heroine returning to the sea.
• In every version Marwood recorded, the teller was a woman.
• Folklorist Tomas Rehn recorded 87 versions of "The Lantern Ox," a tale from mountain farms in central Slovenia.
• Most versions of "The Lantern Ox" end with a family moving to a new valley.
• In every version Rehn recorded, the teller was a woman.
choices: Marwood recorded 212 versions of "The Salt Bride," more than twice the 87 versions of "The Lantern Ox" that Rehn recorded.
Whereas most versions of "The Salt Bride" end with a return to the sea, most versions of "The Lantern Ox" end with a move to a new valley.
In every recorded version of both "The Salt Bride" and "The Lantern Ox," the person telling the tale was a woman.
In every version Marwood recorded, "The Salt Bride," a tale from coastal northern Portugal, was told by a woman.
explanation: The goal asks for a similarity, so first look for the one feature the two blocks of notes share: in every recorded version of each tale, the teller was a woman. Choice C states that feature and uses "both" to apply it to the two tales together, so it does exactly what the goal asks.

A.why: You picked the choice that works out the gap between the two collections. "More than twice" is a difference, not a similarity, so this choice compares the tales without doing the job the goal names.

B.why: Everything in this choice is accurate, but "whereas" tells you it's built on a contrast between the two endings. The goal asked for something the tales have in common.

D.why: This choice names the shared feature, but only for "The Salt Bride." It never says the same is true of "The Lantern Ox," so no similarity is actually stated.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two warm-up routines. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Kinesiologist Dana Pruitt tested two warm-up routines on 40 college sprinters.
• The first routine, a series of dynamic leg swings, lasted 12 minutes and required no equipment.
• The leg-swing routine improved the sprinters' 30-meter times by an average of 0.08 seconds.
• The second routine, a series of weighted-sled pushes, lasted 6 minutes.
• The sled routine improved the sprinters' 30-meter times by an average of 0.08 seconds.
choices: The leg-swing routine lasted 12 minutes, which made it twice as long as the 6-minute sled routine that Pruitt tested.
The leg-swing routine and the sled routine each improved the sprinters' 30-meter times by an average of 0.08 seconds.
Unlike the sled routine, which required a weighted sled, the leg-swing routine Pruitt tested required no equipment at all.
Pruitt's sled routine improved the sprinters' 30-meter times by an average of 0.08 seconds in just 6 minutes.
explanation: Scan the two routines for what they share before you read the choices. They differ in length and equipment, but each improved 30-meter times by the same average of 0.08 seconds. Choice B names both routines and uses "each" to give them that shared result, so it emphasizes the similarity.

A.why: You answered a question about the gap between the routines. "Twice as long" measures a difference in length, which is the opposite of what the goal asks for.

C.why: "Unlike" marks this as a contrast. It accurately says the routines differ in equipment, but the goal was a similarity.

D.why: This choice gives the 0.08-second result for the sled routine only. It never says the leg-swing routine matched it, so the reader never sees the two routines side by side.

stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two species' migrations. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ornithologist Priya Velan tracked tagged shorebirds flying south from breeding grounds in western Alaska.
• Western sandpipers weigh about 25 grams.
• Velan's tagged western sandpipers spent the winter on the coast of Peru.
• Whimbrels weigh about 400 grams.
• Velan's tagged whimbrels spent the winter on the coast of Brazil.
• Birds of both species made a single refueling stop, at Grays Harbor in Washington State.
choices: Whereas Velan's tagged western sandpipers spent the winter in Peru, her tagged whimbrels spent the winter in Brazil.
At about 400 grams, a whimbrel weighs roughly sixteen times as much as a western sandpiper, which weighs about 25 grams.
Velan's tagged whimbrels made a single refueling stop, at Grays Harbor in Washington State, on their way south.
On their way south, Velan's tagged western sandpipers and whimbrels both refueled once, at the same Washington harbor.
explanation: The notes about the two species run in parallel and mostly differ, in weight and in where the birds spent the winter. The one shared point is their migration route: both made a single refueling stop at Grays Harbor. Choice D names both species and uses "both" to state that shared stop, so it emphasizes the similarity.

A.why: "Whereas" sets up a contrast between the two wintering grounds. The fact is accurate, but it's a difference, and the goal asked for a similarity.

B.why: You were drawn to the precise calculation. "Sixteen times as much" measures the gap between the birds' weights, which shows how different they are, not what they share.

C.why: This choice gives the shared feature, but only for whimbrels. Because it never says the western sandpipers made the same stop, no similarity is stated.
